slop.title: Slop
slop.definition: A result of missing judgment: the agent substituted a default, broke something already approved, or left a defect or unfinished work.

bad-tone.title: Bad tone
bad-tone.definition: Dishonest or disrespectful communication with a person: pressure, manipulation, dark patterns or false signals.

instruction.title: Instruction
instruction.definition: How the agent works: permissions, scope and the order of checks. It is not directly visible on screen and is verified through the process.

project-decision.title: Project decision
project-decision.definition: A specific approved decision of one product that results are compared against. Deviating from it is slop under US-008. Project decisions stay with their project and are not part of this public canon.

records.title: Explicit requirements outrank generic style lists
records.statement: Follow the user's current explicit requirements when they differ from general style preferences. Review how well the requested design works and how it uses the project's design system. Do not reject an intentional choice merely because it appears in a generic anti-pattern list.

records.title: Needed additions are proposed; execution is proactive
records.statement: When the agent believes an element outside the request is needed, it sends a separate proposal with the element's purpose and a preview instead of adding it to the result (UR-1). Inside the authorized scope, technical steps, checks and fixes of defects against the stated intent are done without asking, and signals such as risks, contradictions or lost elements are raised without asking. Outside that scope, or when a step is irreversible or external, the agent reports and asks first.

records.title: Verify the actual result before handoff
records.statement: Before presenting a revision, verify the actual result against its requirements. Check design-system use, behavior and visual output separately. Reading guidelines or passing a build is not evidence that the interface meets its acceptance criteria. Use an independent reviewer before handoff. The reviewer gets the result and the original requirement, not the author's plan or explanations, and judges what is on screen. A finding is backed by a screenshot of the state it describes; a pass or a failure that is only expected, not seen, is not evidence. Each theme the product supports, such as light and dark, is checked on its own: a pass in one theme does not prove another.

credits.name: Benji Taylor
credits.work: Stageshow: references/review.md (The reviewer's brief); references/craft.md (Color and looks)

records.title: Fix systemic issues at the design-system source
records.statement: Make a systemic fix in the governing design-system component, token or recipe. Use its existing API or a defined extension, then verify the consuming interfaces. Do not conceal a local override behind a new token name.

records.title: Design-system changes inside authorized work
records.statement: A change to the design system does not by itself require renewed permission for work the user has already authorized. Ask when an unresolved product or design choice needs the owner's decision, and stay within the authorized scope.

records.title: Visual recipes stay project-scoped
records.statement: Keep a project's visual recipes scoped to that project. Reuse the principle of consistency without turning a particular color, shape or treatment into a universal requirement.

records.title: Keep provenance of examples and claims
records.statement: Preserve the provenance of examples, references and claimed results. Distinguish a recorded example from a live verified run, and an agent proposal from an owner-approved decision. State missing evidence explicitly.

records.title: Leave everything outside the change intact
records.statement: Preserve approved content, behavior and composition outside the requested change. Compare the original requirement, the baseline and the candidate. Treat unverified areas as unknown rather than passed.

records.title: No agent or process service notes on production pages
records.statement: Production pages of any project do not show the agent's or the process's service notes: verification dates, internal source IDs, blocks such as "Sources, checked" with a date, or lines such as "Sources:" followed by internal IDs. Facts are checked against fresh sources, but that evidence lives in the working records. Sources meant for readers, such as sources in science or medicine, or citations, are not forbidden.

records.title: Product-wide removal covers every occurrence
records.statement: When asked to remove a pattern throughout a product, locate and update every occurrence in the agreed scope. Verify the affected routes and components before handoff instead of fixing only the example that was pointed out.

records.title: An existing page is the approved baseline
records.statement: A page that existed before the current task is the approved baseline for an audit or a fix of it (US-001, US-008). The typefaces, palette, motifs and motion it uses consistently, meaning the same treatment for the same role in two or more places or a reused class, token or component, count as its design system only where one of these rules makes an exception for the approved design system: decoration (DEC-1), lines (DEC-2), labels above headings (DEC-7) and monospace type (KR-19). Every other rule applies as written, with its own counter-examples. Only what is already on the page counts: the agent does not declare signatures, and an element it added, a one-off or an inconsistent use is judged by the rule as written. The baseline protects an element only while it passes the role test of US-012: it does a job for the reader here, such as marking a real sequence, a state or the product's own idea, and no more fitting element would do that job better. Repetition alone does not pass the test: decoration that does no job, or whose job a more fitting element would do better, is fixed under US-012 however consistently it repeats, and a treatment that matches the Example of the rule it would be exempt from never enters the baseline. A page generated in the current task is not a baseline. The baseline never covers these always-findings, which stay findings on any page and are fixed, not only reported: fabricated proof, numbers and promises (DEC-5); a pill or badge above the H1 (DEC-7); a sparkle, wand or gradient chip as a generic sign of AI (ST-2; the product's own registered icon excepted); claims about competitors without a verified source (XP-22b); agent or process service notes (US-009); placeholder or service text (XP-33); text contrast below WCAG AA, 4.5:1 or 3:1 for large text (DEC-6, XP-18), and input boundaries or icons below 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11); text too small to read on a phone, such as body text below 14px; touch targets smaller than KR-3 allows. How to fix: the content items of that list (proof, numbers and promises, the pill, the AI sign, competitor claims, service notes, placeholder text) are removed or replaced; restyling one, or turning a pill into a text label, is not a fix. Contrast, size and touch-target defects are restyled (US-012). A fabricated item stays only when the user supplies its source; the one case that waits for the user's answer is the one DEC-5 names. How to check: before judging, list the always-findings and the generic tells and keep them out of the baseline; then list every other element the page uses consistently, each with the places it repeats, and apply an exception only to listed elements. A report that keeps an always-finding as part of the system, or leaves it as an open question, is a finding. Example: a landing page whose monospace captions and plain-text section kickers repeat across its sections keeps them (KR-19, DEC-7), and a pricing page for a review tool keeps its comment-pin motif across hero, badge and call to action, while a "NEW" pill above the headline and an invented "2,400+ teams" are fixed, and "01/"–"04/" on a list of contact links are replaced by icons that say where each link goes (US-012). Not a finding: keeping a consistent pattern that the baseline list names, when it is neither an always-finding nor a generic tell.

records.title: Restyle first, remove last
records.statement: Fix a defect by changing how the element looks or behaves: its contrast, size, spacing, a shadow or color token, the bounds of its motion, its reduced-motion state. Remove an element only when the element itself is the defect, or when the user asked to remove it. Role test: for an element a fix would touch, and for decoration the baseline repeats, name the job it does for the reader here. If it does none, or a more fitting element would do it better for the user, replace it with that element, or with the plainer page when that does the job; a removal names what does the element's job now. If it already is the most fitting option, it stays. The content always-findings of US-011, such as fabricated proof, a pill above the H1, a service note or placeholder text, are such defects: they are removed or replaced, and restyling them is not a fix. A fix applies in the same way to every element of the same group, or to none of them: removing the border of one link in a list and keeping the borders of the others is a finding. How to check: for each changed element, name the defect by rule ID and the smallest change that removes it; a removal that a restyle would have fixed is a finding, and so is any loss without a named reason. The report ends with a table: element, kept / changed / removed, and the rule ID behind each change. Example: numbers "01/"–"04/" on a list of contact links replaced by icons that say where each link goes; a background grid that marks nothing replaced by the plain background; 10px captions raised to a readable size and kept in their typeface; a muted text color darkened until it reaches 4.5:1 instead of removing the text; every row of a link list changed the same way. Not a finding: numbered steps of a real process keeping their numbers; a product's own motif kept; removing fabricated testimonials (DEC-5); removing an element the user asked to remove.

records.title: Ship only requested content
records.statement: Do not invent content. Text, data, claims, features, people, quotes, logos and numbers that a person will read as fact ship only if the request, the approved layout or the existing page contains them; content already on a page does not exempt proof and claims from DEC-5. A request covers only its own content: placeholder rows or invented items inside a requested block are unrequested. Approval of a direction, a discussion or a reference unlocks proposals, not implementation. Each invented item in a delivered result is a finding; repeating it after a correction raises its severity. This rule is never a reason to remove parts of an existing page, such as its navigation, footer, actions, sections, illustrations or motifs; on an existing page, new elements, sections and decoration are proposed, not added (US-002). The visual treatment of requested content (type, color, motion, an illustration of the product) is design work judged by the interface rules, not by this one; sample data inside a product illustration is not a claim unless it presents customers, quotes or results as real. Not a finding: text the user supplied verbatim; the navigation, footer and primary action that a page of the requested kind needs, when their labels claim nothing the request lacks. Proposals and execution follow US-002.

records.title: Concentric radii for nested shapes
records.statement: Derive nested corner radii from each other instead of picking them by eye: inner radius = outer radius − padding, or outer = inner + padding. An inner radius equal to or larger than the outer one is a finding.

records.title: Touch targets on touch screens
records.statement: On touch screens every interactive element has a hit area of at least 44×44 px, and the hit areas of neighboring elements do not overlap. The desktop recommendation is KR-3d.

records.title: Desktop hit areas for key actions
records.statement: On desktop, a 44×44 px hit area is only a recommendation for key actions. Hit areas of 15 px or more inside menus and similar lists are not a finding.

records.title: Optical, not arithmetic, centering
records.statement: Center asymmetric shapes, such as a play triangle or an icon inside a button, optically, preferably inside the SVG itself. Arithmetic centering that looks off-center is a finding. A text label centers by its visible letters, not by its line box: an untrimmed line box also holds the font's space for ascenders, accents and descenders, which is rarely even around the capitals, so a label centered by its box usually reads off-center, most often low. This shows in a button with an icon and a label, in a pill or badge, and in an initial inside an avatar. Trim the text to cap height and baseline (text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic) or offset it in the component. In a centered price the digits are what is centered; the currency sign is placed outside that box. Example: a check icon and the word "Sent" in one button, the word visibly lower than the icon. Not a finding: the same button with the word trimmed so its capitals line up with the icon's center.

records.title: Shadow for layers, border for state
records.statement: Show that a card or popover sits on its own layer with a shadow from the design system's tokens, not with a 1px solid border. Keep borders for states such as focus or selection, and for places that do not read without one. Unlike the source recipe, a 0-blur ring shadow counts as a border (DEC-2); whether an edge is needed is decided by DEC-2.

records.title: Line breaks follow the sentence
records.statement:
A heading that fits the available width stays on one line; a narrow max-width or a
must not force a break. When it does not fit, it breaks at a sentence boundary, after the full stop, or between meaningful word groups, never in the middle of a phrase. text-wrap: balance on a short heading made of several sentences is a finding: it evens out line lengths and ignores the syntax. Content paragraphs use text-wrap: pretty, so no orphan is left on the last line. Custom typographic compositions are not a finding. Example: "Stop scrolling. Start / your workflow." on a desktop screen where the heading fits on one line. Not a finding: "Stop scrolling. / Start your workflow." where the width runs out.

records.title: Press feedback scales to exactly 0.96
records.statement: A pressed button responds with scale(0.96); no feedback and a deeper squeeze are both findings.

credits.work: Details that make interfaces feel better (make-interfaces-feel-better skill)

records.title: Icon stroke matches the adjacent text
records.statement: An icon's stroke width matches the stroke of the text next to it. Calculate it where possible and propose adjusting the icon stroke or slightly changing the font weight; next to bold text, prefer a filled icon instead of adding another stroke width. There is no fixed stroke value. Icons on one screen share one family and one stroke width. Within one group of icons, such as a toolbar or a navigation list, filled and outlined styles are not mixed: the group is filled or outlined as a whole, next to bold text preferably filled. A single filled icon among outlined ones is a finding unless the design system assigns the filled style to a state such as selected. The icon size stays with the design system. Example: three navigation icons from one card, one filled and heavy, two thin outlines. Not a finding: the same three drawn the same way, with even visual weight.

records.title: Interactive motion can be interrupted
records.statement: Use CSS transitions for interactive states where a person can change their mind mid-motion, such as opening and closing a menu. Keep keyframe animations for one-off sequences.

records.title: No animation on first render
records.statement: Do not play an entrance animation every time the page loads unless the entrance is intended. An intentional entrance stays as designed. Not a finding: a one-off product demo, such as a terminal that plays a deploy or a card that types a suggestion, that plays once, does not delay reading or using the page, and shows its final state at once under prefers-reduced-motion.

records.title: Duration follows the weight of the action
records.statement: Give direct feedback a short duration (100–160 ms) and context changes a longer one within the motion budget. One duration for every transition is a finding.

records.title: Smooth scrolling without breaking scripted scroll
records.statement: Do not rely on html { scroll-behavior: smooth } when the page scrolls from code: in embedded viewers scrollTo() and scrollIntoView() may not move the page. Implement smoothness in JavaScript and confirm arrival; if scrollY has not changed after 400 ms, jump to the target.

records.title: Monospace type only where explicitly allowed
records.statement: Monospace type is not slop in itself, but AI-generated interfaces overuse it, so treat it as slop by default. Use it in code blocks and inline code in technical text, in terminal or CLI commands shown for copying, and in diff or patch views. Elsewhere, including IDs, numbers, labels, tags, headings and interface elements, it is a finding unless it is one consistent layer for one role: the same monospace treatment for one kind of text everywhere that kind appears on the page, such as all metadata captions, or the voice of a developer tool's own output. Monospace for a second role, or mixed into headings and body text, is a finding. Numerals in regular text never use monospace digits; code and that one layer keep their own digits (TY-1).

records.title: Hover highlight needs a click
records.statement: A row or card that changes color on hover must do something on click. Either make it clickable or remove the hover highlight. Not a finding: a tooltip, crosshair or value readout that appears on hover over a chart or a data point; the hover itself shows the data.

records.title: Disclosure needs a visible indicator
records.statement: A details/summary disclosure whose default marker was removed shows a chevron or plus sign that changes state when it opens, so the row does not read as a caption. Size the summary's hit area per KR-3 on touch screens and KR-3d on desktop.

records.title: Indented lists keep their markers
records.statement: A plain prose list that is indented shows visible markers; indentation without markers reads as shifted paragraphs, often after a CSS reset such as ul { list-style: none }. Classed navigation lists without markers by design are not a finding.

records.title: Icon transitions transform instead of swapping
records.statement: In projects that already have animated icon toggles (menu and close, play and pause, arrows and chevrons), icons of the same shape in another orientation (arrows, chevrons, plus and cross) change by rotation; interpolating coordinates between them bends the lines. Where a transformation is intended, a coordinate morph or a crossfade of two SVGs is a finding. The check is manual: an agent does not notice on its own that a transition looks wrong, so a person sets the boundary. Otherwise a plain crossfade between icons is not slop in itself and requires neither morphing nor an animation library.

records.title: Font smoothing chosen per typeface and size
records.statement: Choose font smoothing for each typeface and size. Do not set one smoothing value, such as -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased, on the root for every typeface.

records.title: Image outlines only as an option for content images
records.statement: For images that are part of the content, such as images inside an article, a thin low-opacity 1px outline may be offered as an option, never required. An outline around images anywhere else is slop. Transparent images and images the author intentionally integrated with their surroundings are not a finding.

credits.name: Jakub Krehel
credits.work: Details that make interfaces feel better (make-interfaces-feel-better skill)

records.title: Prose on all-caps display pages stays in normal case
records.statement: On a page that sets display text in capitals, prose gets its own class with text-transform: none and the text typeface. A global text-transform rule on body does not remove the need for that class.

records.title: Plain font numerals in regular text
records.statement: Regular text uses the font's ordinary numerals. Do not use tabular figures (tabular-nums, tnum), a slashed zero (slashed-zero, zero) or monospace digits in it. Monospace text where KR-19 allows it, such as code, keeps its own digits. Not a finding: tabular figures scoped to amounts, prices, counters and table columns whose digits must line up, such as a ledger or a timer; set on the body or on whole paragraphs, they are a finding.

records.title: No false urgency
records.statement: Interface copy does not create urgency the product does not have, such as an invented deadline or a claim that only a few places are left without data behind it. A real deadline with a date is not a finding.

credits.name: Nick DiLallo
credits.work: This is good UX writing (UX Collective)

records.title: No placeholder or service text in production
records.statement: Service and temporary text does not reach the visible production interface: template default placeholders, a loading state that never loads, aria-only text shown on screen, notes for developers. An empty field hides its element or stops the build. A real empty state with useful text for the user is not a finding.

records.title: Stage shows exactly what production will show
records.statement: Stage must look like a ready candidate for production: what a person sees on stage is exactly what they will see in production. Anything visible on stage that slips through review can be carried into production. Show no commit hashes, preview or stage labels, environment badges or build versions on screen. Identify a build only invisibly: an HTTP header, a build.json file, a meta tag or an HTML comment. The rendered stage and production differ in visible text only by the changes of the release.

records.title: Machine formats translated for people
records.statement: Do not show machine formats such as cron expressions, ISO 8601 durations or raw timestamps to people; translate them into plain language, for example "daily at 06:30 UTC". Leave an unfamiliar format as it is: an invented interpretation is worse than the raw string.

records.title: Compare products at the level of intent
records.statement: When comparing products or writing promotion, compare what each product is meant to do. Do not use internal version numbers, release states or target/today markers.

records.title: Only verified claims about competitors
records.statement: State a claim about a competitor only with a verified source; where there is no verified fact, show a dash. Convey the advantage through the wording of your own product's intent.

records.title: Use the approved positioning in comparisons
records.statement: Before building a comparison or a promotional page, read the product's approved positioning and show its axes. A comparison assembled from technical mechanisms that omits the agreed differentiation is a finding.

records.title: Structure before decoration
records.statement: Carry grouping, hierarchy and separation with space, type and alignment first, then with background. Add a line, container, shadow, badge, icon tile or gradient only when the content does not read without it, when it marks a state or an interactive boundary, or when the approved design system defines it. Test by hand: remove the element; if nothing is lost, it is a finding. Replacing one decoration with another (a border with a ring shadow, a card with a tinted box) is the same finding. The removal test covers the decorations this rule names; it is not a reason to remove an illustration, a section or motion, which other rules judge (US-012). On a page that existed before the task, decoration it uses consistently counts as its design system (US-011) while it passes the role test of US-012. Example: a section card holding cards, each with lines between its rows. Not a finding: an input boundary, a focus state, decoration the approved design system defines.

records.title: Lines only where structure needs them
records.statement: A border, divider, outline or ring shadow is not the default way to group content: use spacing, type and background first. Remove a line when switching it off changes neither grouping, interactivity nor state, or when two other cues already mark the same edge. Keep lines for input and control boundaries, focus and selection, dense data tables, images that blend into the background (KR-9), and lines the approved design system defines. A framed box inside a framed box is a finding; input fields and controls inside a frame are not, because their boundaries are among the exceptions above. Any visible line up to 2px counts as a line under this rule: border, outline outside :focus-visible, box-shadow with 0 blur and a positive spread, hr, 1–2px pseudo-elements, divide-x and divide-y. Lines between list rows belong only in dense data where the eye follows a row across columns; when space already separates the rows, the lines are a finding. Check by hand in order: remove, look for a substitute, look for double encoding, apply the exceptions. Detection signals (share of framed containers, nesting depth, double encoding, lines between rows, line density, a border with a wide shadow) only prompt a review and give no verdict: their thresholds are not calibrated. Example: a rounded-xl border shadow-sm section holding three rounded-xl border cards, each with divide-y. Not a finding: a settings group without frames, where spacing separates the groups and inputs have a 3:1 boundary (WCAG 1.4.11).

records.title: Cards are not the default container
records.statement: A container with a border or shadow and with a radius or background, that is a card, is only for a real object: one that is dragged, clicked as a whole or has its own state (a kanban item, a product). A card inside a card is a finding; input fields and controls inside a card do not count as cards. Example: every section of the page wrapped in a card. Not a finding: selectable option tiles, such as plan or habit choices shown as tiles with a selected state; each is clicked as a whole and has its own state. Detection signal: a card inside a card, or cards in more than half of the page's sections. Detection signals only prompt a review and give no verdict: their thresholds are not calibrated.

credits.work: AI slop catalog

records.title: Shadows only for real layers
records.statement: A shadow means a layer above the content. Use it for a real layer or when the approved design system defines it. A shadow on an element that is not a layer is a finding, including a shadow used in place of a border that DEC-2 would remove. Real layers: popovers, menus, modals, sticky elements, dragged objects, and a card that really is a layer above the content (KR-5). Example: a shadow on every card and section by default. Not a finding: a product mock, screenshot or device frame shown lifted above the page with one shadow; it presents an object, so it is a real layer. Detection signal: a shadow on any other element. Detection signals only prompt a review and give no verdict: their thresholds are not calibrated.

records.title: No fabricated proof
records.statement: Show metrics, testimonials, client logos and claims about the product, such as user or star counts, version numbers, pricing terms and promises like "no card required", only from the product's data, the request or material the user supplied, with a source. An item without such a source is fabricated, and that is a finding, on an existing page too (UR-1): template defaults, items that contradict the repository or the data, and invented people, quotes and logos are the common cases. How to fix: remove the item or, when its section would be left empty, replace it with a marked slot such as "[Customer quote: name, role, link]". A slot is service text under XP-33, so the page does not ship until real content fills it. Marking the item for review instead is not a fix (US-011). The one exception is a live product whose people wrote the item, shown by the user saying so or by the repository's history: then it is a finding that needs its source, and it stays until the user answers. A page an agent or a template produced never takes this exception. Example: "10,000+ teams", "3x faster", a row of reviewer avatars or a row of logos in a template with no data behind it. Not a finding: a metric from product data with its source; a testimonial with a name and a link; a fact the user supplied. This extends LK-01 and XP-22b to claims about one's own product. Detection signal: numbers with "+", "%" or "x" without a source in the data, a testimonial without a name or a link. Detection signals only prompt a review and give no verdict: their thresholds are not calibrated.

records.title: Muted text needs a role and contrast
records.statement: Use muted text only for truly secondary meta information and with at least the WCAG text contrast: 4.5:1 for regular text, 3:1 for large text. Muting everything secondary by default is a finding. Example: every description under headings in regular-size gray text at 3:1. Not a finding: the date and author under an article at 4.5:1. Detection signal: a large share of text nodes below the WCAG threshold for their size or using a muted token; gray text on a colored background. Detection signals only prompt a review and give no verdict: their thresholds are not calibrated.

records.title: Labels above headings only as a system
records.statement: Use an eyebrow, kicker or section numbering above a heading only as a deliberate element of the brand system or for a real sequence of steps. A label above every heading by default is a finding, and so is numbering such as "01/" on items that are not a real sequence: it is replaced by what does that job better, such as icons that say where each link goes (US-012). A pill or badge above the H1, meaning a chip with a background or border and a radius that holds short status text such as "NEW", "v1.4" or "Booking projects", is a finding on any page, including one that uses pills elsewhere (US-011). Fix it by removing the pill and moving any real information it carried, such as a version or availability, below the H1 or into the body, for example a version next to the install command. Turning the pill into a text label above the H1 is not a fix: the space above the H1 stays free unless the page already had a plain-text kicker there that carries no status. Example: "01 / FEATURES", "02 / PRICING" above every section; a "NEW" pill with a dot above the hero headline. Not a finding: one deliberate kicker of the brand system, set as plain text in the page's own type and carrying no status such as "NEW", a version or availability; real steps of a process. Detection signal: two or more sections with a small uppercase label above h2, or a pill above the H1. Detection signals only prompt a review and give no verdict: their thresholds are not calibrated. Related: UR-1.

credits.work: AI slop catalog

records.title: No identical feature grids with icon tiles
records.statement: Three or more identical blocks of an icon in a colored tile, a heading and text give everything the same weight; this template is a finding. Example: "three features" with icons in squares. Not a finding: truly equivalent options (pricing tiers, comparisons); selectable option tiles in a form or an onboarding step, each a choice with a selected state; iconography the design system defines and that carries meaning. Detection signal: neighboring containers of the same size and structure, a 32–128px icon tile right before a heading, one icon per card. Detection signals only prompt a review and give no verdict: their thresholds are not calibrated.

credits.name: impeccable.style
credits.work: AI slop catalog

records.title: Decorative gradients and glow only from the design system
records.statement: Gradient text, a purple-to-blue gradient and colored glow on a dark background are allowed only as brand identity fixed in the design system; otherwise they are a finding. Example: a purple gradient hero heading in a project without such a brand. Not a finding: a brand gradient defined by design-system tokens. Detection signal: background-clip: text with a gradient, hues 250–290 in a hero background, a colored blurred shadow on a dark background. Detection signals only prompt a review and give no verdict: their thresholds are not calibrated.

records.title: No gray text on colored backgrounds
records.statement: On a colored background, such as a brand or accent fill, text is white or black. To mute it, lower the opacity of that white or black, for example rgb(255 255 255 / 0.6); never use a gray token or a gray hex value. Accent-colored text is the only exception. Muted text still meets the contrast in DEC-6. Example: #aaa text in a purple table cell. Not a finding: white text at 0.6 opacity in the same cell when it meets that contrast.

records.title: Icons come from one chosen set
records.statement: Interface icons come from the product's own icon set (its icon component, sprite or icon package) or, where the product has none, from one published set picked deliberately. A glyph drawn ad hoc for one screen is a finding: its weight and drawing differ from the icons around it, and it is among the most visible signs of generated UI. How to check: trace every icon on the screen to its set; an inline SVG path that belongs to no set, or icons from two sets on one screen, is a finding. Example: a settings card whose three icons are improvised shapes in tiles of three different hues, one filled and two outlined. Not a finding: the same three icons from the product's set, one stroke width and one color, with status carried by color alone. An icon drawn because no set has that symbol is allowed when it follows the set's grid and stroke; KR-11 covers stroke and family.

records.title: AI features are named by what they do
records.statement: An AI feature is labelled with the action it performs, such as "Summarize thread" or "Explain the failure". A sparkle, a magic wand or a star as a generic AI sign, a gradient "AI" chip, or purple used as the color of AI is a finding: it says only that AI is involved, not what will happen. A sparkle that is the product's own registered icon is allowed: it is the product's mark, not decoration. Gradients and glow are also covered by DEC-9. How to check: read the label of every control that starts an AI feature with its icon hidden; a label that does not say what happens is a finding. Example: a failed deploy card with a wand button and a gradient chip reading "AI". Not a finding: the same card with a plain button reading "Explain the failure".

records.title: No near-touching edges
records.statement: Neighboring edges of boxes, surfaces, text blocks and corners either line up exactly or sit clearly apart, by at least the layout's gutter and never less than 8px. A gap of 1 to 3px looks unintended and is a finding. How to check: measure the distance between adjacent edges in the rendered layout, horizontally and vertically, corners included; a gap above 0 and below 8px between surfaces that are not meant to touch is a finding. Example: a confirmation toast whose top edge stops 2px below the panel it belongs to. Not a finding: the toast aligned to the panel's edge, or set 12px below it. Spacing inside a component that the design system defines, such as the gap between an icon and its label, is not a near-touch.

records.title: No layout jumps on state change
records.statement: When an element is added, removed or changes its content, nothing around it jumps. A new row moves the content below it together with its own height, or its space is reserved in advance; a button keeps one width across its states (for example "Save", "Saving…", "Saved"), sized for the longest; a popover or menu has its final size before it appears and keeps its position against its trigger while it is open. How to check: trigger each state change and compare the frames before, during and after; a neighbor that moves in one step, a button that changes width, or an open surface that resizes or drifts from its anchor is a finding. Example: checking a task inserts a status line and the next row snaps down. Not a finding: the next row moves down together with the opening space, or the space was reserved.

records.title: Sentence case by default
records.statement: Headings, labels, buttons and menu items use sentence case: a capital on the first word and on proper names only. Title Case and letter-spaced capitals are allowed only where the brand or design system defines them as a style, for the roles it names, or where the platform's own convention requires them. How to check: read every heading, label and button; Title Case or tracked capitals with no design-system style or platform convention behind them are a finding. Example: a card titled "RECENT DEPLOYS" in tracked capitals with a button reading "View All Logs". Not a finding: "Recent deploys" and "View all logs", or tracked capitals on labels when the design system defines that label style. Prose on all-caps pages is covered by C-11, labels above headings by DEC-7.

records.title: Emoji are content, not interface icons
records.statement: Emoji belong to content, such as messages and reactions. An emoji in the place of an interface icon, in navigation, buttons, list markers, feature lists or status, is a finding, in a playful style too: a playful style changes the shape of the icons, not their kind. How to check: search markup and copy for emoji characters and check where each one renders; one inside a control, a heading or a list marker is a finding. Example: a pricing list whose items start with a green check emoji and a sidebar item whose label starts with a bar-chart emoji. Not a finding: the same list with check icons from the product's set, or an emoji reaction on a chat message.

records.title: No invented logo
records.statement: A product appears with the mark it actually uses, or with its name set in type when it has none. A letter or symbol in a colored square or circle made up to stand in for a logo is a finding, and so is a look-alike of another company's logo; other companies' logos come only from their real files, unaltered in shape and color. How to check: trace every logo on the page to a source file from the brand; a mark with no source is a finding. Example: a header with a white letter in a purple rounded square next to the product name. Not a finding: the product name set as a text wordmark when no mark exists. Customer logos used as proof are covered by DEC-5.
